name: Lidia Al-Zogbi
title: Assistant Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering
fitReason: New 2026 Assistant Professor with a strong CS-facing perception, spatial reconstruction and robotic autonomy portfolio. Full prior-institution methods establish real neural-perception-to-robot planning; a nonclinical software/phantom project would be the appropriate inquiry scope.

physicalEvidence.summary: AURA-CVC, first posted July 2025 and published February 2026, uses Dense-UNet anatomical landmarks to generate scanning paths for an actual UR10e, then learned vessel segmentation to select and revisit an insertion pose. Its vessel model builds on Al-Zogbi’s first-author temporal-memory TransUNet work. Ten commercial-phantom scenarios produced ten successful first-attempt needle placements, but insertion is supervised: a person marks the vessel center once and the needle tip after each step for a proportional controller. This is real JHU-era hardware, not a patient trial or fully autonomous needle tracking. Current Tufts apparatus is unverified, hence physical 20. Separately, full 2026 Perseus integrates SAM2 adapters, DepthAnythingV2 and DROID-SLAM for endoscopic reconstruction; video experiments and offline scale registration do not independently establish robot-action execution.
